bios.mihai-margineanu: Few Romanian artists are recognised from the first chords as fast as Mihai Margineanu — the singer-storyteller who turned humour, irony and the characters of the Romanian mahala into a genre of his own. Songs like «Zaritza», «Paraschiva» and «Foaie verde, foaie fragă» are sung in chorus at every show, and his double career — musician and much-loved actor, known from the hit series «Las Fierbinți» — has earned him an audience that crosses generations. On stage with his band, Margineanu delivers a show where the stories between the songs are awaited as eagerly as the songs themselves — and the room goes home feeling it shared a table with a friend.
bios.vlad-corb: Raised in Transylvania and trained at the acting school in Bucharest, Vlad Corb writes songs like monologues: rock with folk roots, on lyrics where mythology blends with confession. The «Prometeu», «Orfeu», «Persefona» series brought him his first loyal audience and proved that sung poetry in Romanian can sound contemporary, not dusty. Influenced by Radiohead, Muse and Jeff Buckley, he builds concerts with theatrical intensity — from whisper to explosion — and a direct, almost intimate bond with the room. An artist at the start of a long road, of the kind you listen to with the lights off.
bios.white-mahala: White Mahala started in 2014 from one simple, contagious idea: the mahala street party, played on rock instruments and without a trace of irony — pure joy, fully embraced. Founded by actor Ovidiu Niculescu, the band turned «O mie de pahare» into a party anthem with tens of millions of views, while songs like «Băutura (mă face deștept)» and «Cântă mahalaua» keep the floor full from weddings to downtown clubs. Live, White Mahala is a Balkan carnival: brass, choruses sung by the whole room and an energy that leaves no one seated — the reason their parties are remembered.
bios.omul-cu-sobolani: Since 1997, out of Constanța, Omul cu Șobolani (OCS) has crossed Romanian alternative rock with the same unmistakable voice: Dan Amariei, a frontman who writes about the city, loneliness and revolt with self-irony. Songs like «Copilul rebel», «Razna», «Oda» and «Cine e de vină» have become classics of the genre, and the band's catalogue has passed the hundred-song mark — grunge, alternative and pop-rock melted into a sound of their own. After almost three decades on stage, OCS remains a constant live presence of Romanian rock, with an audience that now brings its children along — the surest proof the songs have passed the test of time.
bios.lupii-lui-calancea: A bass player and producer from the Republic of Moldova, Alex Calancea started Lupii lui Calancea in 2017 with a clear mission: authentic folklore, performed with respect and pushed into the present with modern rhythms, all the way to drum'n'bass. The collaborations with Surorile Osoianu — «Purtata», «La Portiță» — have gathered tens of millions of views and carried the folk song to an audience that had never been near folklore, from Arenele Romane to the big festivals. Live, the Wolves sound like an electric hora: untouched tradition, contemporary groove and an energy that fills festival squares and concert halls alike.
bios.ratb: Robin and the Backstabbers brought into Romanian rock a poetry nobody had sung this way before: the provinces, the trains, the failed loves and the cold sun, run through guitars and through Robin's voice. The «Bacovia Overdrive» trilogy — from «Stalingrad» to «Arhanghel'sk» and «Vladivostok» — became a landmark of local indie, and songs like «Soare cu dinți», «Sat după sat» and «Natașa» are sung word for word at their shows. On stage the band swings between melancholy and catharsis, between the whispered verse and the loud guitars — the reason their concerts have become rituals the audience returns to, year after year.
bios.the-kriptonite-sparks: Formed in Botoșani in 2009, while still in high school, The Kryptonite Sparks grew show by show until «Și golanii beau ceai» became an arena chant and a no. 1 in the Radio Guerrilla chart. Indie rock sung in Romanian, with humour, jagged guitars and lyrics about adolescence and small towns — confirmed by the debut album «ERAI /// Eterna Reîntoarcere A Identicului». The band has played Electric Castle and Summer Well, toured abroad, and their live shows — with improvisation, accidental stand-up moments and a crowd that knows every line — have become the trademark of a band impossible to confuse with anyone else.
bios.nuante: Out of Pitești, Nuanțe sing about love, longing and finding your way back, in a Romanian alternative rock where melody matters as much as distortion. Four albums — the most ample, «Peren», with eleven songs — have built an audience that fills clubs across the country on every tour, while «Roi de fluturi», «Raiul tău» and «Eva» have gathered hundreds of thousands of organic listens, with no radio formulas. Nuanțe are proof that sincerity sung in Romanian finds its audience: direct lyrics, choruses that stay with you and concerts where the crowd sings the second voice from the first chord to the encore.
bios.bob-ramanka: Bob Ramanka is the alter ego of Timișoara musician Bogdan Cotîrță Gruicin, known from the band Melting Dice — a project where trip-hop, minimalist electronica and spoken poetry meet in Romanian. Songs like «Granulat», «Trage» and «Vorba Bună» sound like journals set on a beat: introspection, the city and emotion filtered digitally, with a carefully built aesthetic. The project lives equally well in headphones and on stage — including in unexpected formats, such as the concert with a string quartet — and brings a rare shade to the roster: music to listen to closely, not just to dance to.
bios.adi-istrate: A promise in the course of keeping itself: ADI ISTRATE, artist and songwriter of Romania's new generation. He studied composition and voice at the Irish Institute of Modern Music in London and plays drums, guitar, bass, piano and marimba. Audiences first met him as a member of pop band Maxim, and his solo career took shape after the first season of One True Singer, where he stood out both as a vocalist and as a songwriter. With more than 450 shows across the country and big-stage appearances alongside international artists such as James Arthur and Willy William, ADI has earned a reputation as an authentic performer and versatile artist, ready for the most important events.
bios.alb-who: Few producers on Romania's electronic scene are busier than Albwho, known for a sound that joins modern house with strong club energy. He has built a solid portfolio through releases such as "Jumatate Goala", "Labirint" and "Chupapi" (with Jo), plus successful remixes for some of Romania's biggest artists — "Facem cum vrei tu" (Delia), "Tare" (Antonia) and "Lacrimi si Pumni in Pereti" (Carla's Dreams). His constant presence in the line-ups of major festivals such as Untold, Neversea and AWAKE confirms his status as an energetic performer whose sets are built for the dancefloor.
bios.albert-nbn: Romania's new trap wave claims a handful of defining names, and Albert NBN is among them — an authentic style with deep roots in local urban culture. He quickly shaped a distinct identity built on realness and ambition, supported by a large community of active fans on TikTok, YouTube and Instagram, with strong engagement at every release. His songs mix international influences with a distinctive local sound, and his presence on stage and in videos has turned him into a reference point of the Romanian trap scene. Internationally, collaborations with names such as French Montana and Swae Lee confirm his global potential.
bios.alina-eremia: Radio charts have known her for a decade: Alina Eremia, a constant presence of Romanian pop, on streaming and on stage. She represented Romania at Junior Eurovision at 12, and at 18 became known to the wide public through the lead role in the hit series "Pariu cu viata". Her music career took off in 2014 with the hit "Cum se face", followed by a long run of successful songs that gathered millions of fans. With a recognisable voice, a modern pop aesthetic and a hitmaker's track record built over more than a decade, Alina remains one of the most solid presences in Romanian pop, with dozens of hits to her name.
bios.ami: A powerful voice and hits that led Romanian radio for years have made AMI a name pop audiences mistake for no one else. Born in Baia Mare and devoted to music since childhood, she built a distinct artistic identity, with charisma and a stage presence of her own. Her mainstream breakthrough came with the hit "Deja Vu", together with Grasu XXL — one of the most played songs on Romanian radio, with millions of views and recognition at the Media Music Awards. The success continued with a series of releases that confirmed her as a hitmaker and a safe choice for events and festivals.
bios.andre-rizo: On the Romanian dance scene respect is earned in years — and Andre Rizo, DJ and producer, has had it for two decades. Raised next to a musician father, he entered the industry in 1999 and officially began his DJ career in 2006, as a resident of the famous Pacha Club in Bucharest. In the years that followed he devoted himself to studio production, working on his own material as well as for many other dance artists. A defining moment was the EP "Going Forward", the ninth of his career, a period in which he became one of the most played DJs and producers of the moment. Beyond clubs and festivals, Andre constantly finds new forms of artistic expression.
bios.andrei-ursu-wrs: Andrei Ursu is an artist on a continuous rise, known internationally through the wrs project — which carried Romanian music onto European stages — before returning to his real name. He won audiences with hits such as "Noaptea ne fura iubiri" (with Theo Rose), a no. 1 in the radio charts, and "De-ai fi in locul meu", a Top 3 entry, along with memorable collaborations such as "Sa ma iubesti" (with Eva Timush). With millions of views online and concerts built on storytelling, romance and a direct connection with the audience, Andrei Ursu delivers authentic live experiences and remains one of the most charismatic presences of the new pop generation.
bios.andrew-dum: A rising star of electronic music, Andrew Dum is a native talent of the mix, with a bold style that brings people together. His sets mean cool grooves, fresh melodies and catchy vocals. He was the first Romanian DJ with a national tour — X Tour, which crossed 12 of the country's most important cities and closed with three special shows in Dubai. He has played a private Louis Vuitton party and a Coca-Cola Worldwide event, and his track "Limoncello", with Michel Kotcha, earned support from EDM names such as Hardwell, Don Diablo and Lost Frequencies. A constant presence on the Untold and AWAKE stages, Andrew Dum is pure energy.
bios.antonia: Antonia's voice is recognisable within a second — a distinctive timbre, a powerful stage presence and hits that led the radio charts and streaming platforms for years. She grew up in the United States, in Utah and Las Vegas, where she studied music and worked in modelling with international agencies such as Ford Models — influences that shaped her modern, cosmopolitan pop style. Back in Romania at 18, she began her career alongside producer Tom Boxer: debut single "Roses on Fire" and the hit "Morena" propelled her quickly, and the long series of successful songs that followed established her for good.
bios.babasha: Fresh and hard to pin down, Babasha brought the new Romanian wave a blend of his own: modern urban, Oriental and Balkan influences. Two consecutive songs were named "Song of the Year" on Spotify Romania — "Baklava" and "Cat Vrei Tu" — while the album "Atipic" received the "Album of the Year" title. The hits "Baklava" and "Pai Na" each passed 120 million streams, confirming his impact on the public. He has worked with some of Romania's biggest artists, from Antonia and INNA to Delia, and his live shows, built with a full band and festival energy, recommend him for any big stage.
bios.bad-and-boujee-party: When the night calls for hip-hop culture, the crowd knows where to look: Bad and Boujee Party, the club event series with an electric atmosphere. The party combines trap, hip-hop, dancehall and R&B into a night dedicated to dancing and the hits of the moment, with a bold, spectacular vibe. Since launch, the concept has gathered a loyal audience and reached some of the country's most famous clubs and event spaces. More than a simple party, Bad and Boujee is an entertainment brand that brings urban-luxury energy and aesthetics to the dancefloor — the young crowd's pick for a memorable night.
bios.bvcovia: A dark, melodic sound and a personal take on rap — these are the foundations on which Bvcovia built his place in Romanian trap and hip-hop. After early years under the name MCHH, he shaped the Bvcovia identity and reached an ever-wider audience through songs such as "Sange pe pat si pe podea", "Nu Te Mai Recunosc", "Praf" and "Dala Dumla", as well as many collaborations across the urban scene. Projects such as "Vise Lucide", "En Sabah Nur 2" and "BANDO 4" mark his evolution, and on stage his music takes on a direct, intense energy, fit for festival, club and concert audiences alike.
bios.carlas-dreams: No one has pushed nonconformism further in Romanian music than Carla's Dreams — an anonymous identity, versatile songs and powerful messages, with millions of fans and hundreds of millions of views. "Sub Pielea Mea #Eroina" won over international markets too, climbing to no. 11 on Shazam worldwide, above names like P!nk and Coldplay. The "Nocturn" project — six stories told by six characters across roughly 200 days — brought songs such as "Luna", "Dependent" (with Deliric) and "Anxietate" (with Antonia). With hundreds of concerts and a rare ascent, started in Moldova and consolidated in Romania, Carla's Dreams remains a landmark of alternative pop.
bios.chris-hype: Chris Hype is a Romanian electronic music DJ and producer, known for the energy of his live sets at parties and festivals across the country. He made his mark on the Romanian electronic scene through collaborations and remixes with artists such as Alexia T, Doria, Keo and Alexandra Ungureanu, and his rebranding as Chris Hype opened a new artistic direction with the single "Hold My Love" — a celebration of love, life and music. He has played live at festivals such as Senzoria (Iasi), alongside Manuel Riva, at events pairing music with visual art, and remains a safe choice for events that need energy and authentic hype.
bios.dan-gerosu: Dan Gerosu is a rap artist with a long record: he first took the stage in 1997, and in 2007 founded the group Sagrada Familia together with Bughi, Bufu and DJ Twist, releasing the album "Gangsta" in Cluj. Since 2015 he has continued solo, collaborating with some of the biggest names in Romanian hip-hop culture — Ombladon, Cheloo, Bitza, Freakadadisk, Alan & Kepa, DJ Wicked and Phunk B. After a long series of singles, the album "Monstru" confirmed his status as an active veteran of the genre. On stage, whether at a festival or in a club, Dan Gerosu takes concerts to the next level — and genre audiences have quickly become loyal to him.
bios.deliah: DELIAH is a DJ known for elegant, atmosphere-driven sets that carry a room from sunset until late into the night. With a fine sense of selection and an unmistakable presence behind the decks, she has played rooftops, lounges and day parties across the country, including opening some of Romania's most sought-after electronic events. She is the kind of DJ who reads the room before leading it: she builds gradually, with clean transitions and a clear direction for the evening, without cheap tricks. That is why she is chosen both for refined private events and for big stages — anywhere the atmosphere matters as much as the music.
bios.emaa: EMAA's voice resembles nothing else in her generation — a complete artist and songwriter who carries her audience into a cinematic sound universe where emotion, poetry and live energy meet. She began writing poetry and prose in high school, and today turns that sensibility into personal, unmistakable lyrics. She shaped her identity working with important producers and artists such as Silent Strike, Deliric, Carla's Dreams and The Motans, and the wide public discovered her with the success of "Insula". Since then she has climbed steadily in the radio charts and remains one of the most appreciated live presences of her generation.
bios.erika-isac: The Romanian music industry has few voices as fresh as Erika Isac. A finalist of the first One True Singer season, she launched alongside ADI with the single "Regreti", supported by the country's most important radio stations. With over seven years of industry experience, she has built a solid fan base through collaborations such as "4 dimineata" (with Marko Glass) and "Sugar" (with Theo Rose), as well as the EP "11", made together with ADI. She has written songs for the soundtrack of the film "Haita de actiune" and caused a sensation at Urbanist Sessions. With a special energy and a strong stage presence, Erika is ready for the biggest stages.
bios.eva-timush: From the Republic of Moldova comes a magnetic presence and a voice that wins people over instantly: EVA TIMUSH, a new-generation promise that is hard to overlook. Her path began on The Voice Kids Russia, where she impressed millions of viewers, and continued with Next Star Romania, Romania's Got Talent and The Voice of Romania semifinals. With a steadily growing online community and a fresh artistic identity, she keeps strengthening her position through releases such as "Colegi de apartament" (with Vescan), "Imuni la bine" (with JUNO) and the hit "Fantasy" (with OSCAR). With an authentic style and a special energy, EVA TIMUSH is ready for the big stages.
bios.florian-rus: The new generation of Romanian music counts Florian Rus among its most appreciated artists and songwriters. With an authentic, deeply personal style, he blends pop influences with urban and alternative elements in songs that reach audiences directly. The collaboration "7 Zile", with INNA, confirmed his place at the top of listeners' preferences, while "Strazile din Bucuresti", with Mira, remains one of his most loved projects, cementing his hitmaker status. Beyond his solo success, Florian is also one of the most prolific songwriters of recent years, and his sincere lyrics turn every live appearance into an experience full of emotion.
bios.grasu-xxl: The foundations of Okapi Sound carry Grasu XXL's signature, alongside Guess Who, Vlad Lucan, Mitza and Paco 10Grei. With more than 20 years on Romania's main hip-hop stage, he represents one of the biggest names in the Romanian music industry. Over the years he has released well-known songs both solo and in collaborations — among the most loved: "Turbofin", "Blanadeurs", "Drumul spre Succes" and "Lala Song" — while "Tu, Marie" reached millions of people, digitally and live. With an unmistakable flow and a stage presence to match the name, Grasu XXL remains one of the best performers on the Romanian scene.
bios.guess-who: Guess Who became known to the wide public with the album "Probe Audio" (2009) and the song "Locul Potrivit", a remake of Horia Moculescu's "Noi in anul 2000". The series of socially charged songs continued with "Manifest" and "Onoare", and his portfolio grew with hits such as "Tot Mai Sus", "Decat sa minti" and "Cupidon". He has released three solo albums, plus "In Labirint", the album made with Grasu XXL — one of the best-received records of 2018 — and newer singles such as "Personal", heavily played on radio. A reference lyricist of Romanian hip-hop, with a loyal audience built over more than 15 years.
bios.holy-molly: Holy Molly is a complete creative force — singer, songwriter and actress — established on the music scene with a magnetic voice and an unmistakable lyrical honesty. Her impact was quickly felt internationally too: "Shot a Friend" brought her a gold record and no. 1 in the airplay charts of Poland and the CIS, after successes such as "Menage a Trois" (with Lizot) and "Twinkle Twinkle". At home she consolidated her position with songs such as "Ploua" (with Tata Vlad, no. 1 on radio) and "Totul meu" (with ADI, no. 1 on radio and one of the most used songs on TikTok). Holy Molly remains one of the most dynamic live presences of the moment.
bios.hvnds: HVNDS is a modern metal band from Romania, noted for a sound that joins aggression with emotion and for an intense live show, built in detail to involve the audience from the first beat. The album "Animal" reached no. 1 on Apple Music Romania's rock chart and was launched in front of a sold-out crowd of over 1,000 people, while the single "Vin Viu Plec Mort" entered the soundtrack of the film "Teambuilding". The album "Sintetic" continued the series of sold-out concerts, and "Suflet" (with Delia) opened the road to mainstream collaborations. HVNDS has played the stages of Electric Castle, Untold, Neversea and Beach, Please!, alongside huge international names.
bios.idk: Out of Buzau, IDK (idcash) hit Romania's new trap wave with the force of a phenomenon. His rise was lightning-fast: debut album "NONCHALANT" earned three platinum records, with collaborations alongside Marko Glass, Berechet and Blanco, while "CARTEA JUNGLEI" dominated the hip-hop album chart with songs such as "Cleopatra" and "Porno Pop It" (with Satra B.E.N.Z.). The album "IDCASH" set the record for the strongest weekly debut on Spotify Romania, with over 4 million streams in its first week. Signed to Def Jam Recordings Romania, with hundreds of thousands of monthly listeners, IDK is one of the hottest urban presences.
bios.irina-rimes: Born and raised in the Republic of Moldova, Irina Rimes won Romania over with the song "Visele" in 2016, which climbed to the top of the radio charts. Hits such as "Ce s-a intamplat cu noi", "Bolnavi amandoi" and "Sa nu uiti cat te-am iubit" followed, along with five studio albums each built around its own concept, more than 730 million YouTube views and hundreds of concerts at home and abroad — from London and Paris to the US and Canada. She has been a coach on The Voice of Romania for several seasons in a row, and her tours, from HOME TOUR to the "Descantatele" concert at Arenele Romane, confirm her status as a complete artist of her generation.
bios.killa-fonic: A sonic and stylistic chameleon, Killa Fonic constantly reinvents his language, beliefs and mood — and has shaped the direction of Romania's urban scene for a full decade. Between 2015 and 2019 he was part of Satra B.E.N.Z., on the albums "O$OD" and "O$OD 2", projects that defined Romanian trap and brought the genre into the mainstream. Across his career he has released 13 albums, five EPs and more than 70 singles, steadily evolving from trap toward alternative and experimental territory without losing his audience. Killa Fonic remains one of the strongest live presences of the urban scene, in demand at the country's biggest events and festivals.
bios.la-familia: La Familia formed in 1996, on the streets of the Salajan area of Bucharest's Balta Alba district. Founded by Puya and Tudor Sisu, the group gave birth to a style new for its time and quickly established itself in the Romanian hip-hop landscape. Through attitude, authenticity and a direct message, La Familia became a landmark of urban culture, influencing entire generations. Songs such as "In Realitate", "Portret de Politician" and "Terorist" have gathered tens of millions of views and streams. Today, La Familia is more than an established name: a living project that supports and promotes new artists, keeping the same DNA — real, committed and relevant.
bios.manuel-riva: Featured in the international Billboard charts, DJ and producer Manuel Riva has achieved some of the biggest performances ever reached by a Romanian producer. He is known for hits such as "MHM MHM", "Sacred Touch" and "Miami" — tracks picked up in the playlists of world-class DJs like Tiesto, Fedde Le Grand and Cosmic Gate — and was nominated at the MTV Europe Music Awards as Best Romanian Act. He has collaborated steadily with established artists, from Alexandra Stan to Lindsay Lohan, Misha Miller and Eneli, while "Muzele", with Liviu Teodorescu, set a record in the radio charts. One of Romania's most valuable dance producers and performers.
bios.marko-glass: Romanian trap has a few established new-generation names, and MARKO GLASS is one spoken often — a recognisable sound between rap energy and a personal melodic side. The song "Savana" marked one of the key moments of his rise, and since then he has steadily built his discography through solo projects and collaborations with artists such as Bvcovia, RAVA, M.G.L, IDK and Petre Stefan. Albums such as "BANDO 4" and "Mixed Feelings" expanded the MARKO GLASS musical universe and consolidated his presence on the urban scene. On stage, his songs translate into a direct, intense show, connected to the audience and fit for clubs and festivals.
bios.minelli: Global hits rarely start in Eastern Europe; Minelli has made a habit of them — an artist and songwriter with a distinct pop-dance style. "Rampampam" became a global phenomenon — no. 4 on Shazam Global, no. 1 on Shazam Global Dance and top of the charts in over 17 countries — while songs such as "Mariola", "MMM" and "Nothing Hurts" have gathered hundreds of millions of streams. Beyond her own career, Minelli is also one of the region's most appreciated songwriters, having written for international names such as INNA and Sean Paul. A strong presence, built for the biggest stages and festivals in Europe and beyond.
bios.mira: Since 2012, few artists have been loved by Romania's pop audience as constantly as MIRA. With an unmistakable voice and an authentic stage presence, she has accumulated more than 500 million YouTube views and over 100 million Spotify streams. Hits such as "Strazile din Bucuresti" (with Florian Rus), "Cheia inimii mele" (with DJ Project) and "Fete din Balcani" became anthems for an entire generation. She made her album debut with "MiraDivina", and the independent single "Cu Talpile Goale" climbed to no. 1 in the radio charts. MIRA remains one of the most versatile and energetic pop artists of the moment.
bios.noua-unspe-911: Dark and energetic, NOUA UNSPE's sound established itself quickly in Romania's new hip-hop and trap wave. He drew attention through collaborations with heavyweights of the genre — "Umar La Umar" and "Cartieru a luat-o razna" with Killa Fonic, "DVRKSIDE" (with Nane and RAVA) and "Bonnie & Clyde" (with Nane) — songs that built him a solid fan base. Releases such as "ARCA 11" and "69 DEJA VU" confirmed his rise, and appearances on the stages of major festivals such as Beach, Please!, Untold and Electric Castle prove his live energy. An ever more sought-after presence of the Romanian trap scene.
bios.parazitii: Founded in 1994 by Cheloo, Parazitii is considered by many the most important Romanian hip-hop group. Their first album, "Poezii Pentru Pereti", produced independently in 1995, was only the second rap album ever released in Romania. In the established line-up — Cheloo, Ombladon and Freakadadisk — the group marked entire generations with songs like "Antimilitie" and "Playback", always owning the direct language that brought them countless broadcast restrictions. Their music also reached the soundtracks of films such as "Marfa si banii", "Milionari de weekend" and "Nordrand". Three decades on, Parazitii still fill any venue in Romania.
bios.petre-stefan: Petre Stefan's community is the kind that cannot be borrowed: large, loyal, grown together with Romania's new hip-hop and trap wave. He drew attention with the album "Centaur", which quickly brought him into the public eye, and later consolidated his position with the project "Direct din Tei". Songs such as "Balenciaga", "Sange pe pat si pe podea", "Peter Parker", "Scrum" and "Cateodata" have gathered millions of streams and views, and his constant collaborations with the important names of the urban scene have strengthened his status. Active in concerts and online, Petre Stefan remains a constant, authentic presence of Romanian urban culture.
bios.puya: Respect in Romanian hip-hop is not requested, it is earned — and Puya has it, for the career and for the direct, authentic way he relates to life and to his audience. Co-founder of La Familia, he grew up together with Romania's urban scene and stayed relevant precisely through the courage to call things by their name, with lyrics that reflect reality without filters. Across his solo career he has released landmarks such as "Undeva-n Balkani", "Change", "Vestul Salbatic", "Maidanez" and "Opriti Planeta", gathering millions of views. Beyond music, Puya is a complete artist and a straight-talking man, with a stage presence that always stands out.
bios.randi: Randi's career took off in 2005 with the Morandi project, alongside Marius Moga, which conquered Romania and Europe: 2 million copies sold of the debut album "Reverse", eight no. 1 singles and two MTV Europe Music Awards nominations. Morandi released three albums in three years and enjoyed popularity in more than 20 countries, with hits such as "Angels", "Beijo" and "Save Me". Randi then built a successful solo career — a refined songwriter and a performer of singular elegance — confirming himself as one of Romania's most consistent pop hitmakers and a sought-after presence at the most important events.
bios.rares: From Cluj-Napoca, rares walked into Romanian music through the new wave's front door. His story is atypical: a top law student, he left university for One True Singer — a competition he went on to win. His first major hit, "Naspa" (with Arkanian), went viral and sounded across the stages of the big festivals, from Untold and Neversea to Summer Well. The success continued with "Buchet de trandafiri", alongside Olivia Addams, which climbed to no. 2 in Media Forest. His rise brought him the Best New Artist title at The Artist Awards and a lead role in the film "Romina VTM". An energetic performer, born for the stage.
bios.satra-b-e-n-z: Satra B.E.N.Z. is the first trap project in Romania to enter the mainstream, defining a genre now carried by an entire generation. Initially formed by Lu-K Beats, NOSFE, Keed, Super ED and Killa Fonic, the group released the albums "O$OD 1 & 2", with viral songs such as "#Traparmy", "Satra Se Intoarce" and "Dubai". From a niche phenomenon, Satra B.E.N.Z. became a beloved brand, with collaborations ranging from Loredana and Damian Draghici to ADDA, NANE and Shift. In the current line-up — Lu-K Beats, Keed and Super ED, after NOSFE's sudden passing — Satra remains one of the strongest names of the urban scene and an energetic presence on any stage.
bios.speak: SPEAK has been shaping Romanian pop and electronic music for over a decade. Established in the early 2010s through remixes, he has built a portfolio that moves fluidly between pop, hip-hop, dance, afro-house and Balkan influences, reaching as high as no. 13 globally in the Afro House genre. His catalogue includes more than 90 music videos and releases exceeding 12 million Spotify plays. He has reached the podium of the national charts with hits such as "Amor, Amor", "Lasa-ma-mi Place" and "Timpul", collaborating with big names like Delia, Raluka, Doc, Cabron and Theo Rose. Producer, artist and complete performer, SPEAK remains one of the most versatile presences in Romanian music.
bios.stefania: STEFANIA is a singer, songwriter, dancer, actress and content creator. Originally from Galati and based in Bucharest, she has built a unique identity at the intersection of music, dance and visual storytelling. Her debut came organically, after a cover of "Nentori" posted on YouTube propelled her into the mainstream. Her sound blends commercial pop and dance with Balkan influences, built for streaming and for the big stages. Her career counts more than 90 music videos, millions of Spotify streams and the international hit "Ma Bebe" (with Faydee), with over 30 million views. On stage, STEFANIA means choreography, energy and total show.
bios.tania-turtureanu: Few singer-songwriters of the moment are listened to with the attention given to Tania Turtureanu. She writes her own lyrics and music, with an authentic, deep and captivating style that has turned her into a phenomenon on both banks of the Prut. The album "Iubeste-ma" generated millions of views and constant airplay on radio and television in Romania and the Republic of Moldova, while the show "Barbar Canta Femeia Aceea — Iubeste-ma" sold out every edition in Chisinau and Bucharest, including a second edition with seven new songs and a French version of the hit "Iubeste-ma". The series continued with the show "Ce bine ca esti", received just as warmly by the public.
bios.the-motans: Debuting in 2016 with the single "Tu", The Motans quickly became an unmistakable presence in the Romanian musical landscape, combining alternative influences with a pop sensibility. Singles such as "Inainte Sa Ne Fi Nascut", "Versus" and "August" took the top spot in the radio and digital charts, and the project's releases have passed 700 million streams. With three albums and collaborations with INNA, Delia and Irina Rimes, The Motans has established itself as a leading figure of the industry — "POEM" alone passed 80 million views. No. 1 is a position The Motans is already used to, and its concerts fill venues across the country.
bios.tobi-ibitoye: Tobi Ibitoye is a pop-dance artist born in Nigeria and based in Romania since the age of 15. Raised on gospel music and taught violin by his mother, a professional violinist, he reached The Voice of Romania final in 2015 — the moment that opened his way into the industry. A year later, Forbes Romania included him among the most influential young people under 30, and the song "Loving Me" became a hit on American iHeart radio and entered the local charts. With steady releases, well received internationally too, and a warm, unmistakable voice, Tobi brings to the stage a rare mix of soul, pop and dance energy, appreciated at events of every size.
bios.tussin: A relaxed flow, authentic lyrics and the energy of today's urban sound — the calling card with which TUSSIN represents Romania's new hip-hop and trap generation. Raised in Bucharest, he shaped his musical identity drawing on hip-hop culture and personal experience, combining modern trap with rap and urban-pop influences into a recognisable, accessible sound. His album debut, "Capitanul", gathered more than 25 million streams and views, quickly establishing him as one of the most streamed artists of his generation — and one of the most visible live presences of the new wave.
bios.vescan: Vescan debuted in 2006 in the group Re Vers, and after it disbanded began a solo career, becoming one of the most consistent names in Romanian urban music. Over the years he has released several albums and collaborated with a long list of artists, drawing inspiration from everyday life. His direct style and memorable hooks turned him into a hitmaker with broad public appeal, with numerous songs that dominated the radio charts. With a career of nearly two decades behind him, Vescan remains an energetic, versatile performer, in demand at Romania's biggest concerts and festivals.
bios.zodier: Emotion, story, introspection: out of these three words Zodier built his pop sound, with a sensitivity rare in the new generation. He discovered his passion for music at 10, when he received his first guitar, and influences such as Ed Sheeran, Eric Clapton, Post Malone and The Motans shaped his style. His path began organically, after he sent his own lyrics to The Motans, who invited him to his first working sessions. He has collaborated with producers such as Marci & Sebi, Alex Turcu and Damian Rusu, his song "Albastru rasarit" entered the Top 100 Radio Airplay Romania, and the EP "Ma auzi?" earned him an authentic, steadily growing audience.
bios.bruja: BRUJA is the first female figure to establish herself on Romania's hip-hop and urban scene, with a nonconformist attitude and a powerful, versatile voice that has earned her a solid community. Her debut single "Ia Loc" passed 2 million views on YouTube and ran heavily on radio, while her Urbanist Sessions performance gathered more than 3.4 million views, confirming her strength live. She counts hundreds of thousands of monthly Spotify listeners, and after her warmly received debut album "SALEM" she signed with Def Jam Recordings Romania. BRUJA remains an authentic symbol of female empowerment and a trailblazer of the urban industry.
